>## What this PR does / why we need it:
>
>The E2E test base domain was hardcoded as a default value, making it impossible for CI jobs and developers running tests in different environments to override it without modifying source code.
>
>This change:
>- Reads the `BASE_DOMAIN` environment variable in `test/e2e/util/options.go` to allow overriding the default CI base domain
>- Falls back to the existing `DefaultCIBaseDomain` constant when the env var is not set
>- Excludes KubeVirt platform from the base domain override (KubeVirt uses its own domain logic)
>- Adds comprehensive unit tests covering env var precedence, fallback behavior, flag preservation, and KubeVirt exclusion
>- Uses `t.Setenv` for proper test isolation and cleanup
>
>## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
>
>Fixes https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNTRLPLANE-2787
>
>## Special notes for your reviewer:
>
>The `BASE_DOMAIN` env var only applies when no explicit `--e2e.base-domain` flag value has been provided and the platform is not KubeVirt.
>

🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
test/e2e/util/options_test.go (1)
`52-56`: **Minor: Consider using `os.Unsetenv` for clarity in the fallback test case.** Setting `BASE_DOMAIN` to an empty string technically works because the production code checks `len(baseDomain) > 0`, but semantically the test intends to verify behavior when the env var is *unset*. Using `os.Unsetenv` would make the test intent clearer. However, since `t.Setenv("")` produces the same behavior due to how `os.Getenv` returns empty string for both unset and empty-value scenarios, this is acceptable as-is.
♻️ Optional: Make the "unset" case more explicit ```diff if tc.envValue != "" { t.Setenv("BASE_DOMAIN", tc.envValue) - } else { - t.Setenv("BASE_DOMAIN", "") } + // When envValue is empty, BASE_DOMAIN remains unset (or inherits parent env) + // t.Setenv with "" would also work since len("") == 0 evaluates the same ``` Alternatively, keep the current approach for consistent cleanup behavior.
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. In `@test/e2e/util/options_test.go` around lines 52 - 56, Replace the test's fallback that calls t.Setenv("BASE_DOMAIN", "") with an explicit unset using os.Unsetenv("BASE_DOMAIN") so the test clearly expresses the "env var is unset" scenario; update the block that currently uses t.Setenv to call os.Unsetenv when tc.envValue == "" while leaving the t.Setenv("BASE_DOMAIN", tc.envValue) case unchanged. ```
